title: Idea Contract
description: A single candidate improvement proposed by the Dreamer research agent. Each contract is a read-only proposal that documents a pattern found in project telemetry and a concrete change to consider. The Dreamer never modifies code and never approves its own ideas — every contract stays in the 'proposed' state until a human reviews it.

idea_id.description: Stable identifier of the form YYYYMMDD-HHMM-NNN, where NNN is the 1-based index within the run that produced it. Unique across the corpus.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (UTC) when the contract was produced.

generated_by.description: The agent that authored the contract. Always 'dreamer'.

model_used.description: The reasoning model that proposed the idea (e.g. 'deepseek-chat').

signal.description: The pattern observed in the telemetry that motivates the proposal. Should be specific and falsifiable, not a vague hunch.

proposal.description: The concrete, actionable change to consider in response to the signal. Not a vague suggestion.

category.description: The area of the system the proposal touches.

evidence.description: One or more references to real evidence files, each ideally with a line or line-range (e.g. 'test_output/optimized_v2_report.json:104-107'). Every reference must point to a file the Dreamer actually read; hallucinated evidence is rejected before a contract is saved.

confidence.description: How strongly the available evidence supports the signal.

risk_band.description: How risky the proposed change would be to adopt (regressions, user impact, irreversibility).

estimated_effort.description: Rough engineering effort to implement the proposal.

impact.description: Expected upside if the proposal works as intended.

non_goals.description: What this proposal explicitly does NOT cover, to keep its scope honest.

related_ideas.description: idea_id values of earlier contracts this one builds on or relates to. Empty on the first run.

status.description: Lifecycle state. The Dreamer always emits 'proposed'; only a human may advance a contract beyond this.
